title: Revealing the Hidden Brain, with Shankar Vedantam

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收看《心理学话语》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，

sentences.en: Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: This week, we're doing something a little bit different from our usual conversation with a psychologist about his or her thought-provoking research.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将进行一点与众不同的访谈，而非常规那样邀请心理学家来探讨其引人深思的研究。

sentences.en: Today, I will be talking with a journalist and podcast host who has spent more than two decades bringing psychological and behavioral research to the public.
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与一位记者兼播客主持人对话，他在过去二十多年里一直致力于将心理学和行为科学研究带给大众。

sentences.en: Many of you probably know his work, especially if you subscribe to other science podcasts and if you listen regularly to National Public Radio.
sentences.zh: 你们中的很多人可能都熟悉他的作品，尤其是如果你订阅了其他科学播客，或者经常收听美国国家公共广播电台（National Public Radio）。

sentences.en: I'm talking about Shankar Vedantam, the host and executive editor of Hidden Brain, one of
sentences.zh: 我说的就是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam），他是“隐藏的大脑”（Hidden Brain）的主持人和执行主编，

sentences.en: the most popular science podcasts in the U.S., which receives millions of downloads every week.
sentences.zh: 这是美国最受欢迎的科学播客之一，每周都有数百万次的下载量。

sentences.en: Hidden Brain is also broadcast on more than 400 public radio stations across the country.
sentences.zh: “隐藏的大脑”也在全国400多家公共广播电台播出。

sentences.en: Its mission is to explore the unconscious patterns that drive human behavior.
sentences.zh: 它的使命是探索驱动人类行为的无意识模式。

sentences.en: Recent episodes have covered the psychology of money, the rise of rudeness, and resilience in coping with grief, to name just a few topics.
sentences.zh: 最近的节目涵盖了金钱心理学、无礼现象的增多以及应对悲伤时的复原力，这仅仅是几个主题而已。

sentences.en: Shankar Vedantam has been reporting on human behavior and social science research for more than 25 years.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆报道人类行为和社会科学研究已有25年之久。

sentences.en: He was National Public Radio's social science correspondent from 2011 until 2020.
sentences.zh: 他在2011年至2020年期间担任美国国家公共广播电台的社会科学记者。

sentences.en: Before that, he spent 10 years as a reporter and columnist at the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他在《华盛顿邮报》担任了10年的记者和专栏作家。

sentences.en: He is the author of two nonfiction books, Useful Delusions, The Power and Paradox of the
sentences.zh: 他是两本非虚构类书籍的作者：《有用的错觉：自我欺骗大脑的力量与悖论》（Useful Delusions, The Power and Paradox of the Self-Deceiving Brain），

sentences.en: Self-Deceiving Brain, published in 2021, and The Hidden Brain, How Our Unconscious Minds Elect
sentences.zh: 于2021年出版；以及《隐藏的大脑：我们的无意识大脑如何选举总统、控制市场、发动战争并拯救我们的生命》（The Hidden Brain, How Our Unconscious Minds Elect Presidents, Control Markets, Wage Wars, and Save Our Lives），

sentences.en: Presidents, Control Markets, Wage Wars, and Save Our Lives, published in 2010.
sentences.zh: 于2010年出版。

sentences.en: He has also written plays and a collection of short stories.
sentences.zh: 他还写过戏剧和短篇小说集。

sentences.en: And in the interest of full disclosure, I will tell you, APA has worked with Shankar over the years, occasionally referring him to expert psychologists as part of his reporting.
sentences.zh: 为了充分披露信息，我想告诉大家，美国心理学协会多年来一直与尚卡尔合作，在他的报道过程中偶尔会向他推荐心理学专家。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你今天能来，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure, Kim.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸，金。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢今天邀请我来。

sentences.en: Let's start with a little bit more about your story.
sentences.zh: 让我们从更多关于你的故事开始吧。

sentences.en: One item from your CV that I didn't mention a moment ago is that you have an undergraduate degree in electronic engineering and a master's degree in journalism.
sentences.zh: 我刚才没有提到你履历上的一项内容，那就是你拥有电子工程本科学位和新闻学硕士学位。

sentences.en: How did you find your way to reporting on behavioral science and what has made you stick with it all these years?
sentences.zh: 你是如何走上报道行为科学这条路的，又是什么让你坚持了这么多年？

sentences.en: My background as an engineer helped me in some ways enter science journalism, Kim.
sentences.zh: 金，我作为工程师的背景在某种程度上确实帮助我进入了科学新闻领域。

sentences.en: It allowed me the ability to understand how scientific papers were being written.
sentences.zh: 它让我具备了理解科学论文撰写方式的能力。

sentences.en: Many journalists are highly phobic of anything to do with mathematics.
sentences.zh: 许多记者对任何与数学有关的东西都有高度的恐惧症。

sentences.en: I found myself a little less so.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己没那么严重。

sentences.en: And so I gravitated to science journalism almost from the start of my career.
sentences.zh: 因此，几乎从我职业生涯的初期开始，我就被科学新闻所吸引。

sentences.en: I was actually working at the Philadelphia Inquirer at the time, my first newspaper job.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我当时正在《费城问询报》（Philadelphia Inquirer）工作，这是我的第一份报社工作。

sentences.en: And I realized over as I was working at the Inquirer that some of the most fascinating questions in science had to do with the brain and the mind and human behavior.
sentences.zh: 在问询报工作期间，我意识到科学中最迷人的问题其实都与大脑、心灵和人类行为有关。

sentences.en: And so really, over a period of years, my interest gradually narrowed from covering all of science journalism to focusing predominantly on the mind and mental health.
sentences.zh: 因此，在几年的时间里，我的兴趣确实逐渐缩小，从报道整个科学新闻转向主要关注心理和心理健康。

sentences.en: For about 10 years, when I was working at the Washington Post, I focused a lot on mental health
sentences.zh: 在大约10年的时间里，当我在《华盛顿邮报》工作时，我把很多精力放在了心理健康问题和精神病学上，

sentences.en: issues and psychiatry and covered the questions related to mental disorders and the treatment of mental disorders.
sentences.zh: 并报道了与精神障碍及其治疗相关的问题。

sentences.en: And I would say, subsequent to that, largely as a result of a column that I started writing
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，在此之后，很大程度上是因为我在《华盛顿邮报》开始撰写的一个名为“人类行为部”的专栏，

sentences.en: in the Washington Post called Department of Human Behavior, I became increasingly interested
sentences.zh: 我开始对社会心理学的世界越来越感兴趣，

sentences.en: in the world of the social psychology world, the worlds in which psychology speaks not just to
sentences.zh: 在那个世界里，心理学不仅探讨失调或疾病，还探讨心理学如何解决普通人在日常生活中遇到的各种问题。

sentences.en: disorder or illness, but the way in which psychology can address everyday problems that everyday people are having throughout their lives.
sentences.zh: 所以你最初是在美国国家公共广播电台（NPR）创办了“隐藏的大脑”，但几年前，你决定成立自己的制作公司——“隐藏的大脑传媒”（Hidden Brain Media）。

sentences.en: So you started Hidden Brain at NPR, but a few years ago, you decided to open your own production company, Hidden Brain Media.
sentences.zh: 你为什么决定单干？

sentences.en: Why did you decide to go out on your own?
sentences.zh: 作为老板和创业者，你现在能做什么是在以前的工作中做不到的？

sentences.en: And what can you do now as the boss and an entrepreneur that you couldn't do in your prior jobs?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题，金。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 我是在2009、2010年写的那本《隐藏的大脑》的书。

sentences.en: So I wrote the Hidden Brain book in 2009, 2010.
sentences.zh: 它出版于2010年，我想是的。

sentences.en: It was published, I believe, in 2010.
sentences.zh: 我在2011年加入了NPR。

sentences.en: And I joined NPR in 2011.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，NPR看到了我写的关于隐藏大脑的书，他们对我加入NPR来探讨这些问题很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so in some ways, NPR had seen the book that I had written about the hidden brain, and they were interested in my coming to NPR to explore those issues.
sentences.zh: 因此，“隐藏的大脑”的故事在某种程度上其实始于我加入NPR之前。

sentences.en: So in some ways, the story of Hidden Brain really begins from before I joined NPR.
sentences.zh: 在NPR工作的多年里，我会做一些简短的报道，通常是在《早间新闻》（Morning Edition）节目中，

sentences.en: For many years, while I was working at NPR, I would do short stories, usually on Morning Edition,
sentences.zh: 经常与斯蒂芬·斯基普（Stephen Skeep）或大卫·格林（David Green）对话，讨论有趣的社会科学研究，

sentences.en: often in conversation with Stephen Skeep or David Green, talking about interesting pieces of social
sentences.zh: 通常是心理学，但有时也涉及经济学、政治学和社会学。

sentences.en: science research, often psychology, but sometimes economics and political science and sociology.
sentences.zh: 然后在2015年，部分因为这些简短的报道和片段在听众中非常受欢迎，

sentences.en: And then in 2015, partly because those short stories, those short segments proved to be very popular with listeners,
sentences.zh: 我们决定尝试推出这些短篇故事的长篇版本，这就成了“隐藏的大脑”播客。

sentences.en: we decided to try and launch a longer form version of those short stories, and that became the Hidden Brain podcaSt.
sentences.zh: “隐藏的大脑”在NPR度过了一段美好的时光。

sentences.en: The Hidden Brain had a wonderful run at NPR.
sentences.zh: “隐藏的大脑”广播节目在NPR开播，并继续由NPR发行。

sentences.en: The Hidden Brain radio show launched at NPR and continues to be distributed by NPR.
sentences.zh: 但几年前，我决定在某种程度上探索“隐藏的大脑”在大型媒体组织体制之外的发展可能性，这会很有帮助。

sentences.en: But a couple of years ago, I decided that it would be helpful to, in some ways,
sentences.zh: 原因有几个。

sentences.en: explore the possibilities of what Hidden Brain could become outside the confines of a large media organization.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，其中最主要的原因是，“隐藏的大脑”的故事其实并不是一个关于播客的故事。

sentences.en: And there were several reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 我对“隐藏的大脑”的兴趣，可以说真正始于2007年至2009年在《华盛顿邮报》工作期间，当时我在写一个周报专栏。

sentences.en: But I would say chief among them was that the story of Hidden Brain really was not a story of the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，“隐藏的大脑”的起源其实是一个报纸专栏，然后它变成了一本书，

sentences.en: My interest in Hidden Brain, I would say, really began when I was working at the Washington Post in 2007 through 2009, when I was writing a weekly newspaper column.
sentences.zh: 接着变成了电台上的短篇文章，然后才成为一个播客。

sentences.en: So I would argue that Hidden Brain's genesis was really as a newspaper column, and then it became a book,
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，我对“隐藏的大脑”的兴趣并不仅限于音频。

sentences.en: and then it became short articles on the radio, and then it became a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我感兴趣的是它如何能够应用、你知道的，它如何能够在各种不同的论坛和不同的媒体中触及人们。

sentences.en: But to my mind, the interest that I have in Hidden Brain is not limited just to audio.
sentences.zh: 成为一个独立的组织开启了实现这一目标各种可能性，包括例如探索在电视领域的发展。

sentences.en: I'm interested in the ways in which it can apply, you know, it can reach people in all kinds of different forums and different media.
sentences.zh: 我们正在积极考虑“隐藏的大脑”电视节目会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And becoming an independent organization is opening up all kinds of possibilities to make that happen, including, for example, exploring possibilities in television.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上也在积极思考活动业务会是什么样子，

sentences.en: We are actively considering what a Hidden Brain television show could look like.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，你知道的，有些人想要三分钟版本的故事。

sentences.en: We're actually actively thinking about what an events practice could look like,
sentences.zh: 有些人想要45分钟版本的故事。

sentences.en: where we're actually saying, you know, there are people who want the three-minute version of the story.
sentences.zh: 但也有人可能想要三个星期版本的故事，也就是对某个主题有深度兴趣的人。

sentences.en: There are people who want the 45-minute version of the story.
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能真正服务于这些不同的受众？

sentences.en: But there are people who might want the three-week version of the story, people who have a deep interest in a subject.
sentences.zh: 作为一名创业者真是一次真正的学习经历。

sentences.en: And how can we actually serve these different audiences?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢说，在过去的几年里，我算是“收集”了我的街头MBA，人们有时这么叫它。

sentences.en: Being an entrepreneur has been a real learning experience.
sentences.zh: 这也是一段美妙的经历，不仅教会了我如何经营业务，你知道的，如何雇佣员工，以及确保我们能维持运营。

sentences.en: I like to say that I have sort of collected my street MBA, as it's sometimes called, over the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是挺有趣的经历。

sentences.en: But it's also been wonderful, not just in teaching me how to run a business and to, you know, employ people and to make sure that we can keep the lights on.
sentences.zh: 它还教会了我很多关于我自己以及我自身能力和潜力的认识，可以说是非常具有启发性。

sentences.en: All of those have been sort of interesting experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以“隐藏的大脑”这个词是你创造的，它有着特定的含义，我们的一些听众可能并不是完全理解。

sentences.en: It's also taught me a lot about myself and my own abilities and capacities in ways that it's been quite revealing.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这个词的含义以及你是怎么想出来的吗？

sentences.en: So the term Hidden Brain is one that you coined, and it has a particular meaning, which some of our listeners might not fully understand.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Can you explain what the term means and how you came up with it?
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，“隐藏的大脑”这本书的起源就是我在《华盛顿邮报》写的那个名为“人类行为部”的报纸专栏。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 那是一个每周专栏，我会在其中尝试将正在发生的新闻事件联系起来，

sentences.en: As I said, the genesis of the Hidden Brain book was this newspaper column I was writing at the Washington Post called Department of Human Behavior.
sentences.zh: 无论是伊拉克战争、总统大选还是新闻中发生的任何事情，与有趣的社会科学研究结合起来。

sentences.en: It was a weekly column where I would try and link together things that were happening in the news,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一次迷人的实验，因为每周我都必须在新闻中发生的事情与学术心理学或社会科学世界中的事物之间找到有趣的联系。

sentences.en: whether that was the war in Iraq or the presidential election or whatever was happening in the news with interesting social science research.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我开始注意到的一件事是，许多正在发表的有趣研究表明，人们并没有真正完全理解他们自己的行为和动机。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was a fascinating experiment because each week I had to find interesting connections
sentences.zh: 作为一个认为自己非常理性、深思熟虑、有目标性的人，

sentences.en: between things happening in the news and things that were in the world of academic psychology or the social sciences.
sentences.zh: 我发现这非常令人惊讶，因为我觉得，嗯，其他人可能不了解他们的心思，但我肯定了解我的心思，我也知道我为什么要这样做。

sentences.en: But one of the things that I started to notice, of course, was that a lot of interesting work was being published
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常逻辑性的人。

sentences.en: that suggested that people did not really fully understand their own behavior and motivations.
sentences.zh: 但在《华盛顿邮报》撰写这个专栏的过程中，我意识到我的直觉其实是错的，

sentences.en: And as someone who thinks of himself as being a very rational, deliberate, intentional person,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我内心有很大一部分其实是对自己隐藏的。

sentences.en: I found this very surprising because I felt, well, other people might not know their minds, but surely I know my mind and I know why I do the things that I do.
sentences.zh: 我最终称之为隐藏的大脑的某些元素是出于设计而隐藏的。

sentences.en: I'm a very logical person.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你知道的，即使我尽最大努力去接触我大脑的某些部分，它们基本上也是永久对内省关闭的。

sentences.en: But over the course of writing this newspaper column at the Washington Post, I realized my intuition was,
sentences.zh: 但隐藏的大脑还有其他方面，只是简单地超出了视线范围。

sentences.en: in fact, wrong, that, in fact, there was a vast amount of my own mind that was actually hidden from me.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我没有注意到它们，尽管如果我尝试并努力去关注它们，我是能够做到的。

sentences.en: And some elements of what I eventually came to call the hidden brain are hidden by design.
sentences.zh: 所以“隐藏的大脑”其实是我的一个术语，用来概括这一系列发生在我的意识感知之外的事情，

sentences.en: In other words, you know, even if I try my best to access some parts of my brain, they're basically permanently sealed off from introspection.
sentences.zh: 而这些事情实际上正在影响我的行为、判断和决定。

sentences.en: But there are other aspects of the hidden brain that are just simply out of sight.
sentences.zh: 我发现那个世界令人着迷。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not paying attention to them, even though if I tried and I made an effort to pay attention to them, I would be able to do so.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我仍然觉得这个想法很迷人。

sentences.en: So the hidden brain was really my term to pull together this range of things that were happening outside of my own conscious awareness
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我在自己的人生中所遇到的最具革命性的想法之一，那就是尽管我们觉得自己对自己的内心有着完整而全面的理解，

sentences.en: that was, in fact, influencing my behavior, my judgment, my decisions.
sentences.zh: 但我们的理解实际上是短暂的，可能甚至不是我们内心的大多数。

sentences.en: And I found that world fascinating.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在任何给定的时间，我们内心的绝大部分可能对我们来说都是隐藏的。

sentences.en: And to be honest, I still find that idea fascinating.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们花一点时间来谈谈你从哪里获得节目的灵感。

sentences.en: I think it's one of the most revolutionary ideas I've come by in my own life, the idea that even though we feel as if we have a complete and full understanding of our own minds,
sentences.zh: 你现在有一个8人的团队和你一起工作。

sentences.en: our understanding is, in fact, fleeting and probably is not even the vast majority of our minds.
sentences.zh: 你们所有人每天都在阅读科学期刊来寻找灵感吗？

sentences.en: In fact, the vast majority of our minds are probably hidden from us at any given time.
sentences.zh: 听众会向你发送灵感吗？

sentences.en: Well, let's talk for a minute about where you get the ideas for your show.
sentences.zh: 你在寻找什么，又是什么造就了一期精彩的节目？

sentences.en: You've got a team of eight people right now working with you.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Are you all reading scientific journals every day to generate ideas?
sentences.zh: 我有一个非常棒的团队，他们一直在和我一起工作。

sentences.en: Are listeners sending you ideas?
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人已经和我合作很多年了。

sentences.en: What are you looking for and what makes for a great episode?
sentences.zh: 有些是新人，才华横溢。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人都是非常非常熟练的音频制作人。

sentences.en: I have a wonderful team of people who've been working with me.
sentences.zh: 正如你在制作这个播客时可能体会到的，金，音频制作证明比许多人意识到的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Some of them have been working with me for many years.
sentences.zh: 它实际上有很多有趣的元素，许多细微差别，要把它做好并不容易。

sentences.en: Some of them are new, incredibly talented people.
sentences.zh: 因此，我团队中的许多人专注于音频制作，并思考音频制作的细微差别。

sentences.en: Many of them are very, very skilled audio producers.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队确实也有人在研究研究成果和研究见解。

sentences.en: As you probably gathered in putting together this podcast, Kim, audio production turns out to be more complex than many people realize.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，在过去的15年里，我可以说已经养成了一种日常习惯，即非常定期地阅读学术期刊。

sentences.en: It actually has many interesting elements to it, many nuances to it, and doing it well is not easy.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，我认为我的阅读比许多学术界人士还要贪婪，因为我不局限于某一个领域。

sentences.en: So many people on my team are focused on audio production and thinking through the nuances of audio production.
sentences.zh: 所以我阅读心理学、社会学、经济学和田野调查的期刊。

sentences.en: We do indeed have people working on the team who are also thinking about research and research insights.
sentences.zh: 我阅读得非常非常贪婪。

sentences.en: I, myself, over the past 15 years, I would say have made a daily practice of trying to read academic journals on a very regular basis.
sentences.zh: 我也努力追踪我遇到的有趣文章。

sentences.en: And in many ways, I think I read more voraciously than many people who are in the academy because I don't limit myself to an individual feel.
sentences.zh: 所以在过去的15年左右，我可以说，每次我遇到有趣的文章，我都会把文章保存下来。

sentences.en: So I'm reading journals in psychology and sociology and economics and anthropology.
sentences.zh: 然后我有一个内部的归档系统，允许我通过我设置的一组关键词返回并检索该文章。

sentences.en: I read very, very voraciously.
sentences.zh: 所以即使有些事情是你知道的，在五、六、七、八、十年前发生的，我也能找到这些文章。

sentences.en: And I also try and keep track of interesting articles that I come by.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，金，当涉及到几乎所有事情时，我的记性其实非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So for the past, I would say, 15 years or so, every time I come by an interesting article, I save the article.
sentences.zh: 我对面孔和名字的记性很差。

sentences.en: And then I have an internal sort of archiving system that allows me to go back and retrieve the article with a bunch of keywords that I have set up.
sentences.zh: 我忘记了我昨天做了什么。

sentences.en: So I'm able to find those articles even if something came up, you know, five, six, seven, eight, ten years ago.
sentences.zh: 如果你问我昨天午饭吃了什么，我完全记不起来了。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, Kim, that I have a really terrible memory when it comes to almost everything.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种原因，我对多年前发表的研究研究有着极好的记忆力。

sentences.en: I have a very bad memory for faces and names.
sentences.zh: 这让我们受益匪浅，因为我经常能够看到出现的模式。

sentences.en: I forget what I did yesterday.
sentences.zh: 就在几周前，例如，我向一位同事提到，我遇到了芝加哥一位研究人员的作品。

sentences.en: If you asked me what I ate for lunch yesterday, I have absolutely no recollection of it.
sentences.zh: 在过去的18个月左右，我曾多次接触过他的作品。

sentences.en: But for some reason, I have an excellent memory for research studies that were published many years ago.
sentences.zh: 一旦我开始看到这一点，这就告诉我这里正在发生一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: And this has stood us in good stead because I'm often able to see patterns that come up.
sentences.zh: 这个人正在发表，在这个领域非常多产。

sentences.en: Just a couple of weeks ago, for example, I was mentioning to a colleague that I've come by the work of a researcher in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 让我关注它。

sentences.en: And I've come by his work multiple times in the past, you know, 18 months or so.
sentences.zh: 我开始思考如何将这项工作变成一期“隐藏的大脑”节目。

sentences.en: And once I start to see that, that tells me there's something interesting happening here.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你知道的，很多时候，听众经常带着有趣的问题或故事来联系我们。

sentences.en: This person is publishing, is really prolific in this area.
sentences.zh: 团队成员会提出时代精神中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Let me pay attention to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有人在看约翰尼·德普、安珀·赫德的审判。

sentences.en: I start thinking about ways in which that work can become a Hidden Brain episode.
sentences.zh: 我们就在问自己，我们在“隐藏的大脑”中是否有一个故事可以契合这些问题？

sentences.en: As you say, you know, multiple times, listeners often reach out to us with interesting questions or stories.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，很大一部分是让这些不同的线索和想法流向我们，问题、来自学术界的想法、来自已发表文献的想法、

sentences.en: Team members come up with things that are happening in the zeitgeiSt.
sentences.zh: 来自听众的想法、来自我们自己团队成员关于新闻中正在发生的事情的想法。

sentences.en: You know, someone's watching the Johnny Depp, the Amber Heard trial.
sentences.zh: 我认为艺术就在于弄清楚如何将这些融合在一起，创造出“隐藏的大脑”节目。

sentences.en: And we're asking ourselves, is there a story that we can do at Hidden Brain that speaks to those issues?
sentences.zh: 我希望我能确切地告诉你它是怎么做出来的。

sentences.en: A lot of it is, in some ways, allowing these different strands and ideas to come to us, questions, ideas from the academy, ideas from the published literature,
sentences.zh: 我必须说，事实上，这本身可能就是一期“隐藏的大脑”节目，

sentences.en: ideas from listeners, ideas from our own team members about what's happening in the news.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得那些做事的人实际上并不真正擅长告诉你他们是如何做他们所做的事情的。

sentences.en: And the art, I think, is trying to figure out how to sort of meld these together to create Hidden Brain episodes.
sentences.zh: 有时他们认为自己是专家。

sentences.en: I wish I could tell you exactly how it was done.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你的播客里有迈克尔·乔丹、勒布朗·詹姆斯或斯蒂芬·库里，你问他们，你知道的，你是怎么做的，你在篮球场上做什么？

sentences.en: I have to say that, in fact, that's probably a Hidden Brain episode in and of itself,
sentences.zh: 我并不完全确定他们真的能准确告诉你他们在做什么。

sentences.en: because I feel like people who do things actually are not really expert in telling you how they do the things that they do.
sentences.zh: 所以做某事的一部分能力涉及到的技能，我认为，往往对实际做事的人来说是隐藏的。

sentences.en: Sometimes they think they're experts.
sentences.zh: 有时他们自以为是专家。

sentences.en: You know, if you had Michael Jordan on your podcast or LeBron James or Steph Curry and you asked them, you know, how do you, what do you do on the basketball court?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你把迈克尔·乔丹、勒布朗·詹姆斯或斯蒂芬·库里请到你的播客上，然后问他们，你知道的，你是怎么做到的，你在篮球场上都在做些什么？

sentences.en: I'm not entirely sure they can actually tell you exactly what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定他们能否准确地告诉你他们到底在做什么。

sentences.en: So part of the ability of doing something involves skills that are, I think, often hidden from the person who's actually doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以，具备做某事的能力往往包含一些技能，我认为，这些技能对实际操刀的人来说通常是隐蔽的。

sentences.en: At least those skills are not conscious at a level of saying, here are the specifics, five steps that I'm following.
sentences.zh: 至少这些技能在潜意识层面并没有达到“具体步骤是这样，我正在按这五步做”的程度。

sentences.en: All I can tell you is that we are voracious readers and listeners and observers,
sentences.zh: 我能告诉你的是，我们是如饥似渴的阅读者、倾听者和观察者，

sentences.en: and we're constantly thinking of ways in which these different strands can produce interesting episodes for our listeners.
sentences.zh: 而且我们一直在思考，这些不同的元素如何能为听众制作出有趣的节目。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of interesting episodes, are there any that stand out in your memory?
sentences.zh: 说到有趣的节目，有没有哪期在你的记忆中特别深刻？

sentences.en: And are they the ones that the listeners love, too?
sentences.zh: 它们也是听众们最喜欢的节目吗？

sentences.en: Or do you find that some of the stories that you think are terrific weren't as big a hit with your audience?
sentences.zh: 或者你发现，有些你认为极好的故事，在你的受众中并没有那么大受欢迎？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is actually something that I've been meaning to explore as a Hidden Brain episode at some point.
sentences.zh: 是的，这其实是我一直想在某期《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）节目中探讨的问题。

sentences.en: Because, again, I actually think that that's a really fascinating and interesting question, right?
sentences.zh: 因为话说回来，我真的觉得这是一个非常迷人且有趣的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you would think that creators would be very good at predicting what it is that their audience is like.
sentences.zh: 因为你会认为，创作者应该非常擅长预测受众会喜欢什么。

sentences.en: And I think, in general, that is simply not true.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，总的来说，事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: You know, if it was true, we wouldn't have as many duds as we have in the publishing industry or in the movies, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果这是真的，我们在出版界或电影界就不会有那么多票房惨淡的作品了，对吧？

sentences.en: And the people who are skilled at making things, if they truly understood what audiences want, why would they go out and make failures?
sentences.zh: 而且那些擅长制作东西的人，如果他们真的理解受众想要什么，为什么还要去创作失败之作呢？

sentences.en: Why would they make movies that land with a thud?
sentences.zh: 为什么还要拍出反响冷淡的电影呢？

sentences.en: And the interesting thing, of course, is that when you're sitting in a theater watching a movie, I don't know if this has happened to you, Kim,
sentences.zh: 当然，有趣的是，当你坐在电影院里看电影时——我不知道这有没有在金身上发生过，

sentences.en: but it's happened to me multiple times.
sentences.zh: 但这已经在我身上发生过好多次了。

sentences.en: I can sit and watch a movie, and I know three minutes into the movie that this movie is not going to work.
sentences.zh: 我可以坐在那儿看电影，电影才播了三分钟，我就知道这部电影要砸了。

sentences.en: And I know three minutes into the movie, this movie is a failure.
sentences.zh: 电影放映三分钟，我就知道这是一部失败的作品。

sentences.en: The characters are not too wooden.
sentences.zh: 角色并不算太僵硬。

sentences.en: The plot doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 剧情说不通。

sentences.en: It looks, you know, it's a bunch of stereotypes and cliches.
sentences.zh: 你看，你知道的，全是一堆刻板印象和老套路。

sentences.en: And I have to ask myself, then, how is it that I'm able to sit in a theater within three minutes and know something isn't going to work?
sentences.zh: 我不得不问自己，为什么我能坐在电影院里，在短短三分钟内就知道有些东西行不通？

sentences.en: And there's been a whole team of people who've worked on this movie for like five years, and they've spent $20 million doing it.
sentences.zh: 而一整支团队为了这部电影工作了大约五年，还花了2000万美元。

sentences.en: Why couldn't they see the same thing?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们就看不出来呢？

sentences.en: And in some ways, I think the question answers itself, which is that I think when you're very close to something,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我觉得这个问题本身就有了答案，那就是当你和某件事靠得太近时，

sentences.en: you genuinely lose the ability to see what actually is working and not working.
sentences.zh: 你真的会失去辨别什么在起作用、什么不起作用的能力。

sentences.en: And this is why someone who is an amateur can come into something and say, well, why don't we do it this way?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么外行人能够介入某件事，然后说：“嗯，我们为什么不这么做呢？”

sentences.en: This would make much more sense.
sentences.zh: “这样更有意义。”

sentences.en: And all the professionals say, well, of course we can't do it that way.
sentences.zh: 而所有的专业人士都会说：“哦，我们当然不能这么做。”

sentences.en: That wouldn't work at all.
sentences.zh: “那样根本行不通。”

sentences.en: But I think amateurs are often able to see things because they're able to see with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 但我认为外行人往往能看出问题，因为他们能用崭新的视角去观察。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes this is called the curse of knowledge, of course, which is that the more knowledge you have, the harder it becomes for you to actually see which end is up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有时这被称为知识的诅咒，也就是说，你拥有的知识越多，你就越难看清到底哪个在上、哪个在下。

sentences.en: Because you're so flooded with information and ideas and thoughts that you sort of lose the ability to see something as a novice.
sentences.zh: 因为你被大量的信息、想法和思绪淹没，以至于你某种程度上失去了以新手视角看待事物的能力。

sentences.en: So the short answer to your question is, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以对你这个问题的简短回答是，你知道的，

sentences.en: I think quite regularly people have surprised us in terms of the episodes that they've liked compared to the episodes that we have liked.
sentences.zh: 与我们自己喜欢的节目相比，听众在喜欢的节目上确实经常让我们感到意外。

sentences.en: But in general, I will say that when I think about the episodes, my favorite Hidden Brain episodes, the answer to that question is always very simple.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，当我想起那些节目、我最喜欢的《隐藏的大脑》节目时，这个问题的答案总是非常简单。

sentences.en: You know, when people ask me, what's my favorite Hidden Brain episode, I always tell them that my favorite episode is the one that we're doing next week.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当人们问我最喜欢哪期《隐藏的大脑》节目时，我总是告诉他们，我最喜欢的节目是我们要制作的下一期。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And I only mean that partly facetiously.
sentences.zh: 我这么说并不完全是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: I actually think that that's actually genuinely true.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得这确实是发自内心的实话。

sentences.en: I'm someone personally who sort of lives almost entirely in the future.
sentences.zh: 我个人是一个几乎完全活在未来的人。

sentences.en: So the future is more clear to me than the present and the paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以未来对我来说比现在和过去更清晰。

sentences.en: And I'm always invariably excited by what we have coming down the pike.
sentences.zh: 我总是对我们即将推出的内容感到兴奋不已。

sentences.en: So invariably, I'm more excited by those episodes and the episodes we've published already.
sentences.zh: 因此，相比已经发布的节目，我总是对那些新节目更感兴趣。

sentences.en: Can you give us a hint as to what you're working on now?
sentences.zh: 你能透露一点你现在正在忙什么吗？

sentences.en: When I was talking with your executive producer a couple of weeks ago, Tara Boyle,
sentences.zh: 几周前我和你的执行制片人塔拉·博伊尔（Tara Boyle）交谈时，

sentences.en: she mentioned a piece that you're working on having to do with some dreams that a man had years ago, that one of which came true and one of which he is afraid will come true.
sentences.zh: 她提到你正在制作一个专题，内容与一个男人几年前做过的几个梦有关，其中一个梦成真了，而另一个梦让他感到害怕，担心它也会成真。

sentences.en: Yeah, I won't get into all of the details because I want listeners to listen to this episode.
sentences.zh: 对，我不会透露所有细节，因为我希望听众去收听这一期节目。

sentences.en: This is an episode that, in fact, we've been working on for, I would say, almost two years at this point.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一期我们已经筹备了——可以说是将近两年的节目。

sentences.en: And that's the other interesting thing about Hidden Brain episodes, which is some of them come together in three weeks and some of them take months or even years to put together.
sentences.zh: 这也是《隐藏的大脑》节目的另一个有趣之处，有些节目三周就能成型，而有些则需要几个月甚至几年才能制作完成。

sentences.en: But this is a really unusual story about a man who had two dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个非常寻常的故事，讲的是一个做了两个梦的男人。

sentences.en: And, of course, the dreams were just strange dreams, like all dreams are.
sentences.zh: 当然，就像所有的梦一样，这些梦只是奇怪的梦。

sentences.en: And he dismissed them, except that one of the dreams purported to tell him how long he was going to live.
sentences.zh: 他并没有把它们当回事，但其中一个梦似乎在预示着他能活多久。

sentences.en: And he had these dreams when he was a teenager.
sentences.zh: 他是在青少年时期做这些梦的。

sentences.en: And then he put the dreams out of his mind.
sentences.zh: 后来他就把这些梦抛到了脑后。

sentences.en: And then what happened is some years later, the first dream that he'd had that night, which was also a bizarre dream, came true in almost every way, shape, and form.
sentences.zh: 接下来的事情是，几年后，他在那天晚上做的第一个梦——那也是个离奇的梦——在几乎所有的方面都成真了。

sentences.en: And it made him start to ask himself, is it possible that I was told something that night about my future?
sentences.zh: 这让他开始问自己：那天晚上真的有人向我透露了关于我未来的信息吗？

sentences.en: And is it possible that the second dream, which purported to tell me how long I was going to live, is also going to come true?
sentences.zh: 并且，第二个旨在告诉我能活多久的梦，有没有可能也会成真？

sentences.en: And he reached out to Hidden Brain shortly before the birthday, where his dream had forecast that he was going to die, asking us how to think about these dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 就在他梦中预言自己将要离世的那个生日前夕，他联系了《隐藏的大脑》，向我们询问该如何看待这些梦。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's a fascinating story from a psychological point of view, because it raises really interesting questions about how we think about our own mortality,
sentences.zh: 当然，从心理学的角度来看，这是一个引人入胜的故事，因为它提出了非常有趣的问题：我们如何看待自身的终有一死，

sentences.en: how we think about predictions, how we think about prognostications, how we think about patterns in terms of the things that occur to us.
sentences.zh: 我们如何看待预测，我们如何看待预言，我们如何看待发生在自己身上的事所呈现的规律。

sentences.en: The brain is a pattern recognition machine, as many listeners of your show, I'm sure, are aware of.
sentences.zh: 正如你的节目的许多听众肯定知道的那样，大脑一台模式识别机器。

sentences.en: But how does this affect us in terms of our daily behavior?
sentences.zh: 但这会对我们的日常行为产生怎样的影响？

sentences.en: Do we share these fears with other people?
sentences.zh: 我们会与其他人分享这些恐惧吗？

sentences.en: Do we keep them to ourselves?
sentences.zh: 还是把它们藏在心里？

sentences.en: So I feel like this is an episode that explores so many interesting themes of human behavior,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一期探讨了人类行为诸多有趣主题的节目，

sentences.en: because it has so many different ramifications of how we think about ourselves and our lives.
sentences.zh: 因为它对我们如何看待自己和生活有着许多不同的深远影响。

sentences.en: And it's an episode that I've, you know, I really love this episode, and I can't wait for it to come out in a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，我真的很喜欢这期节目，我迫不及待地想让它在几周后上线。

sentences.en: I am looking forward to it as well.
sentences.zh: 我也很期待。

sentences.en: So let's just switch gears for a minute and talk about your most recent book, which is called Useful Delusions, The Power and Paradox of the Self-Deceiving Brain.
sentences.zh: 那我们换个话题，聊聊你的最新书作，书名叫《有用的错觉：自我欺骗大脑的力量与悖论》（Useful Delusions, The Power and Paradox of the Self-Deceiving Brain）。

sentences.en: I would wager that most people at first blush would say self-delusion is a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，大多数人乍一看都会说自我欺骗是一件坏事。

sentences.en: What kinds of delusions are you talking about when you talk about useful delusions?
sentences.zh: 当你谈论有用的错觉时，你指的是哪种错觉？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think you're going to pick up a pattern here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 我想你会发现一个规律，金。

sentences.en: One of the things that interests me is when I find paradoxes in my own behavior, I often follow them because I say, this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 让我感兴趣的事情之一是，当我发现自己行为中的悖论时，我经常会去探究它们，因为我会说：这很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, and so one of the interesting pieces of research that I've come by in the last,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以在过去——

sentences.en: I would say, five, 10 years is ideas that sometimes behaving rationally doesn't produce the outcomes that you think it's going to produce.
sentences.zh: 可以说，五年、十年里我遇到的一些有趣的研究，是关于这样一种观点的：有时按理性行事并不能产生你预期的结果。

sentences.en: And I feel like I run into this all the time in my own life because I'm a very, very rational person.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我在自己的生活中经常遇到这种情况，因为我是一个非常非常理性的人。

sentences.en: And I find myself befuddled and bewildered when rationality doesn't produce the outcomes that you expect.
sentences.zh: 当理性没有产生预期的结果时，我发现自己感到困惑和迷茫。

sentences.en: So, you know, let me give you the simplest of examples, the controversy we've had in the United States about the efficacy of vaccinations against COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，让我举一个最简单的例子，我们在美国围绕新冠疫苗有效性产生的争议。

sentences.en: To my mind, it seems so self-evidently, blindingly obvious that if vaccines have been developed
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这简直是不证自明、显而易见：如果已经开发出了

sentences.en: that are safe and effective and you have a deadly virus that's raging, a virus that can kill you, of course people are going to want to take those vaccinations.
sentences.zh: 安全有效的疫苗，而此时肆虐着一种能置你于死地的致命病毒，人们当然会想要接种这些疫苗。

sentences.en: You know, it's like you're drowning and someone's throwing you a, you know, a line, a life raft.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像你要溺水了，有人向你抛来一根救生索、一个救生筏。

sentences.en: And of course, you're going to grab it, you know, because you would want to save yourself.
sentences.zh: 你当然会抓住它，因为你会想要自救。

sentences.en: And of course, what we've seen in the last 18 months of the pandemic unfolding is that people, in fact, are not behaving rationally.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在过去18个月的大流行演变中看到的是，人们实际上并没有按理性行事。

sentences.en: And for rationalists such as myself, this has often been, you know, deeply dispiriting and befuddling and bewildering.
sentences.zh: 对于像我这样的理性主义者来说，这往往让人感到深深的沮丧、困惑和迷茫。

sentences.en: And so I've increasingly been drawn to research that purports to ask the question, well, why is that?
sentences.zh: 因此，我越来越被这样一项研究吸引，它旨在探究这样一个问题：为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why is it that people, in fact, do not follow what is the most rational course of action?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们事实上不遵循最理性的行事方式？

sentences.en: What, you know, is it possible that, you know, so one explanation is that people don't follow
sentences.zh: 是什么，你知道的，有没有可能，你知道的，一种解释是人们不遵循

sentences.en: the most rational course of action just because they're silly or they're foolish or they're misguided.
sentences.zh: 最理性的行事方式，仅仅是因为他们愚蠢、糊涂或被误导了。

sentences.en: And that's possible.
sentences.zh: 这也是有可能的。

sentences.en: But of course, our minds are, you know, machines that have been constructed over billions of years of evolution.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们的心智是经过数十亿年进化构建出来的机器。

sentences.en: They're very, very skilled at doing certain things.
sentences.zh: 它们非常非常擅长做某些事情。

sentences.en: And the brains that we have handed down to us from evolution are, in fact, very skilled at solving problems of survival.
sentences.zh: 进化传承给我们的其实非常擅长解决生存问题。

sentences.en: You would think that if there's one thing the brain is really, really good at doing, given
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，鉴于我们是通过自然选择过程产生的，

sentences.en: that, you know, we've been produced by a process of natural selection, the one thing the brain should be really good at doing is surviving.
sentences.zh: 如果说大脑真的非常非常擅长做一件事，那件事就是生存。

sentences.en: Because, of course, all of us come from a long line of survivors.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，我们所有人都源自一条漫长的幸存者血脉。

sentences.en: The fact that you and I exist today is because our ancestors learned to survive.
sentences.zh: 你和我今天之所以存在，是因为我们的祖先学会了生存。

sentences.en: They had brains that allowed them to survive.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有能让自己生存下来的大脑。

sentences.en: And so when you look at the brain, it's in some ways facile to basically say there's something wrong with the brain that causes us not to be able to survive.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你审视大脑时，基本上说大脑有什么毛病导致我们无法生存，这在某种程度上未免过于肤浅。

sentences.en: Because you would think the one thing, again, natural selection would design into the brain is a deep capacity for survival.
sentences.zh: 因为你会认为，自然选择刻进大脑的独一无二的特质，正是强大的生存能力。

sentences.en: And so when I think about this, I start to ask myself, well, then what are the mechanisms in the brain that prompt us towards non-rationality or irrationality?
sentences.zh: 所以当我思考这个问题时，我开始问自己：那么，大脑中是什么机制促使我们走向非理性或不理性？

sentences.en: And is it possible, at least in our evolutionary history, that these brain mechanisms played a useful role?
sentences.zh: 至少在我们的进化史上，这些大脑机制有没有可能发挥了有用的作用？

sentences.en: Is it possible that they actually served us in some kind of useful way in our prior past, in our prior history?
sentences.zh: 在我们的过去、在我们的历史中，它们有没有可能确实以某种有用的方式为我们服务过？

sentences.en: And even though it might not be functional today, that might explain then why it is we have those algorithms of the brain today.
sentences.zh: 即便它在今天可能不再起作用，那也许就能解释为什么我们今天依然拥有这些大脑算法。

sentences.en: So the simplest example to give would be, you know, at multiple points in human history,
sentences.zh: 所以，最简单的例子就是，在人类历史上的多个时期，

sentences.en: but also in the history of other species from whom we are descended, you know, animals faced
sentences.zh: 以及在我们祖先所属的其他物种的历史中，动物在面对饥荒、

sentences.en: huge survival problems when it came to famine, when it came to, you know, acquiring enough calories to stay alive.
sentences.zh: 获取足够的卡路里以维持生命时，曾面临巨大的生存问题。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, our brains are designed to pay very, very close attention to any caloric restrictions that we have.
sentences.zh: 因此毫不奇怪，我们的头脑被设计成会非常非常密切地关注我们所遇到的任何卡路里限制。

sentences.en: Because in our ancestral past, famine was a way that we often died.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们祖先的过去，饥荒是我们经常丧命的方式。

sentences.en: And so even though today many of us live in a sea of plenty when it comes to calories and
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管今天我们许多人都生活在卡路里极其丰盛的环境中，

sentences.en: we're surrounded by junk food and soda and potato chips and all of those things, our brains still
sentences.zh: 周围都是垃圾食品、苏打水、薯片和所有这些东西，但我们的大脑仍然

sentences.en: carry the imprint of what our ancestral brains had, which is a deep fear of famine, a deep fear of not having enough calories to live on.
sentences.zh: 带有祖先大脑的印记，那就是对饥荒的深深恐惧，对没有足够卡路里维生的深深恐惧。

sentences.en: And so our brains in some ways are designed to make us eat, even though we might not actually need to eat, even though in fact eating might not serve us well.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某些方面，我们的大脑旨在驱使我们进食，即便我们实际上可能并不需要吃，即便事实上进食对我们并没有好处。

sentences.en: And so it's an example of how we might have ancient algorithms in our mind that served our
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个例子，说明我们头脑中可能存在一些古代算法，它们曾很好地服务过我们的

sentences.en: ancestors very well, but because the human world in which we live in has changed so dramatically right now, the ancestral algorithms no longer work.
sentences.zh: 祖先，但由于我们生活的人类世界现在发生了如此剧烈的变化，这些祖传算法不再管用了。

sentences.en: And in fact, might not only no longer work, they might actually be counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，不仅不再管用，它们甚至可能是适得其反的。

sentences.en: When you think about the epidemics we have around hypertension or strokes and heart disease, some of that has to do with our lifestyle choices in terms of eating and exercise.
sentences.zh: 当你想到我们周围的高血压、中风和心脏病等流行病时，其中一些就与我们在饮食和锻炼方面的生活方式选择有关。

sentences.en: And that's driven in some ways by these algorithms in the brain.
sentences.zh: 而这在某种程度上是由大脑中的这些算法驱动的。

sentences.en: So similarly, when you think about the ways in which our minds operate, there are many,
sentences.zh: 同样，当你思考我们心智运作的方式时，有许多、

sentences.en: many domains in which, in fact, our minds are designed to have delusions, and you could argue that some of those delusions might in fact be useful.
sentences.zh: 许多领域，我们的心智实际上就是被设计成会产生错觉的，你甚至可以说其中一些错觉实际上可能是有用的。

sentences.en: They're actually productive today.
sentences.zh: 它们在今天实际上是具有建设性的。

sentences.en: And I think the simplest and clearest example of this is in the realm of parenting and parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我认为最简单、最清晰的例子就是在育儿和为人父母的领域。

sentences.en: Because when I know when my own daughter was born many years ago, the day she was born, I was sort of the most special day of my own life.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道，多年前当我的女儿出生时，她出生的那天可以说是我一生中最特别的日子。

sentences.en: But when she was born, I had a firm conviction that not only was she the most special child in the world, I had the sense that she was the most special child in the history of the
sentences.zh: 但当她出生时，我有一种坚定的信念：不仅她是世界上最特别的孩子，我还觉得她是历史

sentences.en: world, that she was the most wonderful and important thing that had ever happened in the history of the universe.
sentences.zh: 上最特别的孩子，觉得她是宇宙历史上发生过的最奇妙、最重要的事情。

sentences.en: Now, clearly, when I thought about that rationally, that has to be a delusion.
sentences.zh: 现在很显然，当我理性地思考这个问题时，这一定是一种错觉。

sentences.en: That cannot possibly be true that my one daughter, when she was born, she was the most special thing that happened in the history of the universe.
sentences.zh: 我这唯一的女儿在她出生时是宇宙历史上发生的最特别的事情，这绝不可能为真。

sentences.en: And of course, when you look around and you find that other parents have exactly the same delusions about their own children, you start to say, okay, this has to be a delusion.
sentences.zh: 当然，当你环顾四周，发现其他父母对自己的孩子也有完全相同的错觉时，你就会开始说：好吧，这一定是一种错觉。

sentences.en: It can't possibly be the case that all these children are the most special thing that happened in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 所有这些孩子不可能是世界上发生的最特别的事情，这绝对不可能。

sentences.en: And then you ask yourself, well, why is it that we have this delusion?
sentences.zh: 然后你问自己：好吧，我们为什么会有这种错觉？

sentences.en: And the answer is, as I have discovered through, you know, 16 years of parenting, parenting is really, really difficult.
sentences.zh: 答案正如我通过16年的育儿经历所发现的那样：养育孩子真的非常非常难。

sentences.en: It's expensive.
sentences.zh: 它代价高昂。

sentences.en: It's time consuming.
sentences.zh: 它耗费时间。

sentences.en: It's stressful.
sentences.zh: 它充满压力。

sentences.en: It's challenging.
sentences.zh: 它充满挑战。

sentences.en: For our ancestors, it often involved incredible risks that often put their own lives at risk to make sure that their offspring survived.
sentences.zh: 对我们的祖先来说，为了确保后代存活，这往往涉及难以置信的风险，甚至常常将他们自己的生命置于危险之中。

sentences.en: And the delusion that we have that our children are extraordinary and special is, in fact, a
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己的孩子非凡而特别的这种错觉，实际上是一种

sentences.en: very useful delusion to have because it allows us to commit the time and the resources and the effort that are needed to successfully raise children to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 非常有用的错觉，因为它使我们能够投入时间和资源，付出成功把孩子抚养成人所必需的努力。

sentences.en: Now, can parents go too far with this?
sentences.zh: 现在，父母在这方面会做得过头吗？

sentences.en: Can you basically believe in the extraordinariness of your children to the point where you actually are encouraging them to do things that are harmful or malevolent?
sentences.zh: 你会不会基本上坚信自己孩子的非凡之处，以至于你实际上在鼓励他们去做有害或恶毒的事情？

sentences.en: You know, there are examples of that where children do terrible things and their parents stand by them because they can't bear to think that their children are bad people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，确实有这样的例子：孩子做了可怕的事情，而父母却坚定地支持他们，因为他们无法忍受自己的孩子是坏人这一想法。

sentences.en: But in general, this is a very useful delusion to have.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，这是一种非常有用的错觉。

sentences.en: Because, of course, if we didn't have this delusion, many of us, if we thought very rationally
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们没有这种错觉，我们中的许多人，如果以成本效益的方式进行非常理性的思考，

sentences.en: in a cost-benefit way, you know, do I really want to invest this much time and effort in the care of somebody else?
sentences.zh: 就会想：我真的想在照顾别人这件事情上投入这么多的时间和精力吗？

sentences.en: Many of us might rationally conclude that we don't wish to do those things.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人可能会理智地得出结论：我们并不想做这些事情。

sentences.en: And, of course, that would not be good for the survival of the species and for the continuation of our genes.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对物种的生存和基因的延续是没有好处的。

sentences.en: And so, that would be a simple example of a useful delusion at work.
sentences.zh: 因此，这将是发挥作用的有用的错觉的一个简单例子。

sentences.en: But it turns out that's one of many kinds of delusions that, in fact, might be irrational
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这只是众多错觉中的一种，它们虽然可能是非理性的

sentences.en: or non-rational, but, in fact, might have a profoundly salutary role for us and our species.
sentences.zh: 或不理性的，但实际上可能对我们和我们的物种起到了深刻的有益作用。

sentences.en: I am sure your daughter is the most extraordinary person on the planet.
sentences.zh: 我确信你的女儿是这个星球上最了不起的人。

sentences.en: You're exactly right.
sentences.zh: 你说得一点没错。

sentences.en: I'm often amazed by the way that you get scientists to tell their personal stories and weave together their work and their lives.
sentences.zh: 我常常对你引导科学家们讲述个人故事、并将他们的工作与生活交织在一起的方式感到惊叹。

sentences.en: How do you get them to open up and reflect in this way?
sentences.zh: 你是如何让他们敞开心扉并以这种方式进行反思的？

sentences.en: And a challenge I think we both share, which is to get them to speak in plain English.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们俩都有一个共同的挑战，那就是让他们用浅显易懂的英语发言。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, it is the case that I think we talked about this actually a little while earlier, which
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上正如我们不久前所讨论的那样，这

sentences.en: is I think when you spend a lot of time learning something and studying something, you're so
sentences.zh: 我想当你花大量时间去了解和研究某样东西时，你对所

sentences.en: attuned to the small nuances of what you're studying, you know, the details of what you're studying, that sometimes it becomes hard, I think, for you to see your life.
sentences.zh: 研究事物的微小细微差别、也就是你所研究事物的细节是如此敏感，以至于有时候，我认为，你很难看清自己的生活。

sentences.en: Your own work as a novice would, as an amateur would.
sentences.zh: 像一个初学者、一个业余爱好者那样看待你自己的工作。

sentences.en: So, for example, I'm often amazed that the researchers and scientists that I speak with do not have a good understanding of what it is about their work that actually would interest
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我经常惊讶于与我交谈的研究人员和科学家并不真正清楚他们工作中究竟有哪些部分会引起

sentences.en: the general public.
sentences.zh: 广大公众的兴趣。

sentences.en: What is it about your work that actually would speak to the general public?
sentences.zh: 你的工作中究竟有什么能引起广大公众的共鸣？

sentences.en: I think many researchers genuinely find it hard to actually answer that question, and they find it hard precisely because they know so much, precisely because, in fact, they
sentences.zh: 我认为许多研究人员确实觉得很难回答这个问题，他们之所以觉得难，正是因为他们知道得太多，正是因为事实上，他们

sentences.en: are so smart and so knowledgeable.
sentences.zh: 是如此聪明和博学。

sentences.en: This is, in fact, the curse of knowledge at work, that if you're used to, you know, talking
sentences.zh: 事实上，这就是工作中的“知识的诅咒”：如果你习惯于，你知道的，与

sentences.en: to other people who are fellow academics, who are also deeply immersed and enmeshed in the field in which you're working, it's difficult to step out of that and speak in a way that
sentences.zh: 其他同行学者交谈，他们也深深沉浸并纠缠在你所从事的领域中，你就很难跳出那个圈子，用一种

sentences.en: is accessible or comprehensible to a general audience.
sentences.zh: 普通受众能够理解或听懂的方式说话。

sentences.en: So, in many ways, I think of Hidden Brain as being a bridge between the academy and the public square.
sentences.zh: 所以，在很多方面，我认为《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）是学术界与公众广场之间的一座桥梁。

sentences.en: I sort of think about the work that we're doing as a service role, that we're trying to translate important and interesting ideas from the academy and make them accessible and
sentences.zh: 我某种程度上将我们正在做的工作视为一种服务角色，我们试图将学术界重要且有趣的理念进行转化，使其平易近人且

sentences.en: relevant to people's lives, to the lives of people who are outside of the academy.
sentences.zh: 与人们的生活息息相关，与学术界之外的人们的生活息息相关。

sentences.en: And I think this work is really important to do because, of course, you know, it's not
sentences.zh: 我认为这项工作非常重要，因为当然，你知道的，在我们的世界中，不仅

sentences.en: just the creation of knowledge that is vital in our world, it's the dissemination of knowledge that is vital.
sentences.zh: 知识的创造至关重要，知识的传播也同样至关重要。

sentences.en: And the public plays a really important role in maintaining and supporting science, right?
sentences.zh: 公众在维持和支持科学方面发挥着非常重要的作用，对吧？

sentences.en: So, taxpayer dollars go to fund universities, they go to fund research institutions.
sentences.zh: 纳税人的钱用来资助大学，用来资助研究机构。

sentences.en: It's really important for ordinary people to feel science is not just some, you know, abstruse thing that's happening in some ivory tower.
sentences.zh: 让普通人觉得科学不仅仅是某些，你知道的，发生在某个象牙塔里的深奥事情，这非常重要。

sentences.en: The work that's been done in the academy actually has relevance to my life.
sentences.zh: 学术界所做的工作实际上与我的生活息息相关。

sentences.en: It actually can make my own life better.
sentences.zh: 它确实能让我的生活变得更好。

sentences.en: And so, there's a really important, I think, function in playing this bridge role between the academy and the public square.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为在学术界和公众广场之间扮演这座桥梁的角色，具有非常重要的功能。

sentences.en: Now, how do you get scientists to talk?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何让科学家们开口说话的呢？

sentences.en: How do you get them to focus on stuff that is of relevance to the general public?
sentences.zh: 你是如何让他们专注于与公众切身相关的事物的？

sentences.en: I think some of this comes down to the trust that I think Hidden Brain has earned within the academy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这部分归功于《隐藏的大脑》在学术界赢得的信任。

sentences.en: We are seen as being a serious show.
sentences.zh: 我们被视为一档严肃的节目。

sentences.en: We're seen as a show that deeply cares about science and takes scientists very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们被视为一档深切关怀科学并极其认真对待科学家的节目。

sentences.en: I think I genuinely have a deep affection and a regard for the science and the scientists that we profile on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 我认为我对我们在《隐藏的大脑》中剖析的科学和科学家确实有着深厚的感情和敬意。

sentences.en: I am someone who reads academic publications for pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我是一个为了消遣而阅读学术出版物的人。

sentences.en: I can think of, you know, spending time on a weekend reading academic papers.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，你知道的，把周末的时间花在阅读学术论文上。

sentences.en: And I think of this as being just as enjoyable as watching Netflix.
sentences.zh: 我认为这和看网飞（Netflix）一样令人享受。

sentences.en: So, I think when I speak with scientists or when we reach out to scientists, they know they're
sentences.zh: 所以，我想当我与科学家交谈或我们接触科学家时，他们知道他们

sentences.en: speaking with an interlocutor who genuinely understands and gets them and actually wants is sort of enthusiastic about the worlds in which they operate.
sentences.zh: 在与一个真正理解他们、懂他们并且实际上对他们所处的世界充满热情的对话者交流。

sentences.en: So, I think scientists have come to trust us in some ways in being able to tell their stories in a way that actually reaches people well.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为科学家在某些方面已经开始信任我们，相信我们能够以真正很好地触达受众的方式讲述他们的故事。

sentences.en: But it is the case that, you know, putting together a Hidden Brain episode and putting together an interview with a scientist often involves extraordinary amounts of background
sentences.zh: 但事实是，你知道的，制作一期《隐藏的大脑》节目以及对科学家进行采访，往往需要投入极其大量的幕后

sentences.en: preparation and work.
sentences.zh: 准备和工作。

sentences.en: And, you know, many of my team members play a very active role in thinking through very carefully, you know, what is the arc of this person's research?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我的许多团队成员在非常仔细地思考以下问题方面发挥了非常积极的作用：这个人的研究轨迹是什么？

sentences.en: How can we best profile it so that it lands in the best possible light so the ideas become the most accessible?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能以最好的方式对其进行剖析，使其以最佳的光芒呈现，从而让这些理念变得最平易近人？

sentences.en: How do we connect this with people's lives in a way that makes people feel like these ideas speak to me?
sentences.zh: 我们如何将这些与人们的生活联系起来，让人们觉得这些理念触动了自己？

sentences.en: One research study that has really spoken to me was conducted some time ago by a researcher, I believe, at Columbia University, Shadong Lin Sigler.
sentences.zh: 有一项真正触动我的研究是由一位研究人员在不久前进行的，我相信她是哥伦比亚大学的Shadong Lin Sigler。

sentences.en: You know, she was talking with, she was presenting research to students about science.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她当时在与学生交谈，在向学生介绍关于科学的研究。

sentences.en: And she told, you know, in this research experiment, some students were told about Albert Einstein and were told, you know, Einstein was one of the smartest people who ever lived.
sentences.zh: 她告诉，你知道的，在这项研究实验中，一些学生被告知了阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦，并被告知，你知道的，爱因斯坦是有史以来最聪明的人之一。

sentences.en: His ideas were so brilliant, even though he was working a century ago, you know, his ideas were so smart that we're still struggling to understand his ideas today, that, you know,
sentences.zh: 他的理念是如此辉煌，尽管他是一个世纪前工作的，你知道的，他的理念是如此聪明，以至于我们今天仍在努力理解他的理念，你知道的，

sentences.en: very, very few people truly understand Albert Einstein's insights.
sentences.zh: 极少数人真正理解阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦的见解。

sentences.en: So that's one group of people.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一组人。

sentences.en: And there's another group of people who are told, you know, about the missteps and foibles
sentences.zh: 还有另一组人，他们被告知，你知道的，关于爱因斯坦犯下的失误、弱点

sentences.en: and mistakes that Einstein made, the times in his life, for example, when he couldn't solve
sentences.zh: 和错误，比如他生活中的那些时刻，当时他无法解决

sentences.en: a problem, when he found that he didn't have the mathematical skills to solve a particular challenge.
sentences.zh: 一个问题，当他发现自己没有解决特定挑战所需的数学技能时。

sentences.en: He had to turn to other people for help in order to be able to solve those challenges.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这些挑战，他不得不向其他人寻求帮助。

sentences.en: And then what Shadong Lin Sigler did was a very simple question.
sentences.zh: 然后Shadong Lin Sigler做的是一个非常简单的问题。

sentences.en: She basically said, if you tell these two versions of the stories of Einstein to students, who ends up being more engaged in science?
sentences.zh: 她基本上是说，如果你把这两种版本的爱因斯坦故事讲给学生听，谁最终会更多地投入到科学中？

sentences.en: Who ends up thinking that science is for them?
sentences.zh: 谁最终会认为科学是属于他们的？

sentences.en: And perhaps the way I'm presenting this makes the answer obvious, but when you present Einstein
sentences.zh: 也许我这样表达让答案显而易见了，但是当你把爱因斯坦呈现为

sentences.en: as a genius beyond all geniuses, whose ideas are incomprehensible to us even 100 years later,
sentences.zh: 超越所有天才的天才，其理念即使在100年后我们也无法理解时，

sentences.en: many students are perfectly happy to say, okay, Albert Einstein was a super smart guy, but
sentences.zh: 许多学生非常乐意说，好吧，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦是个超级聪明的人，但是

sentences.en: they don't think that they can become the next Albert Einstein because they say, I'm still having trouble with my algebra class.
sentences.zh: 他们并不认为自己能成为下一个阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦，因为他们说，我还在为我的代数课烦恼。

sentences.en: You know, I still, I'm having trouble with trigonometry.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我还在，我正在为三角函数烦恼。

sentences.en: How can I possibly, you know, aspire to be Albert Einstein?
sentences.zh: 我怎么可能，你知道的，渴望成为阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦？

sentences.en: On the other hand, when you sort of describe the limitations and challenges that Albert Einstein had, you know, he becomes much more relatable as a character.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，当你描述阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦所具有的局限性和挑战时，你知道的，作为一个角色，他变得更加平易近人、更容易引起共鸣。

sentences.en: And now you sort of say, well, I can relate to who this person is.
sentences.zh: 现在你有点像是说，嗯，我可以和这个人产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And yes, you know, some of his ideas are really difficult to understand, but like me, he struggled.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，他的一些理念确实很难理解，但像我一样，他也在挣扎。

sentences.en: And like me, he had setbacks.
sentences.zh: 像我一样，他也有过挫折。

sentences.en: And like me, he had failures.
sentences.zh: 像我一样，他也有过失败。

sentences.en: And I feel like this is a really important insight in science communication that I think many scientists forget, which is it's important not just to tell people about the insight
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是科学传播中一个非常重要的见解，我认为许多科学家都忘记了这一点，那就是不仅要告诉人们当你到达山顶时

sentences.en: you have when you've reached the top of the mountain, it's really important to communicate
sentences.zh: 所获得的见解，向人们传达

sentences.en: to people the struggle it takes to get to the top of the mountain, because it's the struggle
sentences.zh: 到达山顶所经历的挣扎也非常重要，因为正是这种到达山顶的挣扎

sentences.en: to get to the top of the mountain that in fact is where everybody else is who's listening to that episode.
sentences.zh: 实际上正是收听那期节目的其他所有人所处的状态。

sentences.en: Everybody else who says, I have an insight, but I don't quite know if it's a scientific insight.
sentences.zh: 其他所有说“我有一种见解，但我不太清楚这是否是一种科学见解”的人。

sentences.en: I don't know how to actually take the steps to turn this insight into a rigorous scientific conclusion.
sentences.zh: 我不知道如何真正采取步骤将这种见解转化为严谨的科学结论。

sentences.en: They want to hear about the struggle involved in getting to the mountaintop.
sentences.zh: 他们想听听登上山顶所涉及的挣扎。

sentences.en: And when you think about every good science movie that you've seen, you know, think about movies about great scientists, what you'll find, of course, is exactly the same pattern.
sentences.zh: 当你想到你看过的每一部优秀的科学电影时，你知道的，想想关于伟大科学你会发现的电影，当然，正是完全相同的模式。

sentences.en: The movie doesn't start with the moment of blinding scientific insight.
sentences.zh: 电影不会以电光石火般的科学见解时刻开场。

sentences.en: And the rest of the movie is just as this hagiographic look at sort of someone's brilliant ideas.
sentences.zh: 而电影的其余部分也只是一种对某人辉煌理念的这种圣徒传式的审视。

sentences.en: It always starts with a story of what were the challenges you faced?
sentences.zh: 它总是以一个关于你所面对的挑战的故事开场？

sentences.en: What were the setbacks you faced?
sentences.zh: 你面对的挫折是什么？

sentences.en: What is the story that allows you to basically see, I can understand that this insight was hard won.
sentences.zh: 这个故事能让你基本上看出：我能理解这个见解是来之不易的。

sentences.en: This insight involved significant challenge.
sentences.zh: 这个见解涉及重大的挑战。

sentences.en: It involved a journey.
sentences.zh: 它经历了一段旅程。

sentences.en: I mean, think of any adventure story that you've watched or read or liked.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想你观看过、阅读过或喜欢的任何冒险故事。

sentences.en: You know, you don't start the movie by basically saying, you know, the end has been reached.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你不会在电影一开始就基本说，你知道的，终点已经到达。

sentences.en: The victory has been accomplished.
sentences.zh: 胜利已经取得。

sentences.en: The movie always has to start with laying out what the challenges are.
sentences.zh: 电影总是必须以陈述挑战是什么来开场。

sentences.en: And what you're doing with laying out the challenges is really engaging people in the not just engaging people in the solution.
sentences.zh: 而你通过陈述挑战所做的事情，真正让人们参与到不仅仅是让人们参与解决方案中。

sentences.en: I think this is a really important insight that a lot of people in science communication forget.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是科学传播中很多人忘记的一个非常重要的见解。

sentences.en: The central challenge is not engaging people in the solution.
sentences.zh: 核心挑战不是让人们参与解决方案。

sentences.en: The central challenge is engaging people in the problem.
sentences.zh: 核心挑战是让人们参与问题。

sentences.en: Because once you've engaged people in the problem and then you give them the solution, they're receptive to the solution.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦你让人们参与了问题，然后你给他们解决方案，他们就会接受解决方案。

sentences.en: They basically say, aha, I understand now why the solution is relevant to my life because you've actually taken the time to connect them, connect their lives, their problems with
sentences.zh: 他们基本上会说，啊哈，我现在明白了为什么这个解决方案与我的生活息息相关，因为你确实花时间将它们、将他们的生活、他们的问题

sentences.en: the problem of discovery itself.
sentences.zh: 与发现本身的问题联系在了一起。

sentences.en: So, you have a really unique view as someone outside the field who is very knowledgeable about behavioral science research and you've explained, you know, your attraction to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一个对行为科学研究非常了解的局外人，你有一个非常独特的视角，并且你已经解释了，你知道的，你对它的吸引力。

sentences.en: You've been paying attention to it for years and years.
sentences.zh: 你多年来一直对它给予关注。

sentences.en: So, given that and given all of the string that you save over time looking for patterns, can you talk about what you think are the big topics and trends that we might be seeing
sentences.zh: 鉴于此，并鉴于你随着时间推移为了寻找规律而节省下来的所有精力，你能谈谈你认为我们在近期或远期未来可能会看到的重大主题和趋势是什么吗？

sentences.en: in the near or the distant future?
sentences.zh: 近未来还是远未来？

sentences.en: Yeah, I have to confess, I'm probably not very good at predicting the future.
sentences.zh: 是的，我必须坦白，我可能很不擅长预测未来。

sentences.en: In some ways, there's, I think, a robust psychological science that basically says very few people are good at predicting the future.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为有一门强有力的心理科学基本上表明，很少有人擅长预测未来。

sentences.en: So, if you were to ask me, you know, where are these fields going to go in five years' time or 10 years' time?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你问我，你知道的，这些领域在五年后或十年后会走向何方？

sentences.en: I have to confess, I don't know the answers to those questions.
sentences.zh: 我必须坦白，我不知道这些问题的答案。

sentences.en: I don't quite know who to tell me what are going to be the hot areas in psychology five years from now, 10 years from now.
sentences.zh: 我不太清楚谁能告诉我五年后、十年后心理学哪些领域会成为热门领域。

sentences.en: I think I've learned enough to know that I am not going to be very good at predicting what those things are.
sentences.zh: 我想我吸取的教训已经足够让我明白，我不会很擅长预测那些事情会是什么。

sentences.en: In some ways, I have, let's say, a more modest approach to sort of thinking about my work, and that is to basically pay attention to a lot of different things that are happening
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，比方说，我对思考自己的工作有一种更谦逊的方法，那就是密切关注正在发生的大量不同事情，

sentences.en: and asking myself what's interesting about these lots of different things that are happening.
sentences.zh: 并问自己这些正在发生的大量不同事情中有什么有趣的地方。

sentences.en: And some of those things are more modeSt.
sentences.zh: 其中一些事情更加谦逊。

sentences.en: They're not sort of sweeping changes that would transform an entire field, but it's an interesting body of research that basically says, let's look at sort of this interesting
sentences.zh: 它们不是那种会彻底改变整个领域的巨变，而是一个有趣的研究主体，它基本上说，让我们看看这个有趣的

sentences.en: idea and sort of see where we can go from here.
sentences.zh: 理念，并看看我们能从这里走向何方。

sentences.en: So I think there's, you know, I have lots of interesting, you know, interest in lots of different things.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，我对很多不同的事情都有很多有趣的兴趣。

sentences.en: But if you were to ask me big questions, you know, how is economics going to be transformed in the next 10 years?
sentences.zh: 但如果你问我宏大的问题，你知道的，经济学将在未来10年发生怎样的变革？

sentences.en: You know, how is social psychology going to be transformed in the next 15 years?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，社会心理学将在未来15年发生怎样的变革？

sentences.en: I have to confess, I'm probably not the right person to ask you.
sentences.zh: 我必须坦白，我可能不是最适合问的人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let me throw this at you to sort of close things out here today.
sentences.zh: 好吧，为了今天在这里作个收尾，我把这个问题抛给你。

sentences.en: Given that we live in what I believe is a fairly anti-science, anti-intellectual society right now, how do you account for the popularity of a show like Hidden Brain?
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们生活在一个我认为目前相当反科学、反知识分子的社会中，你如何解释像《隐藏的大脑》这样节目的受欢迎程度？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: And I have to say that if I was being perfectly candid, I have to say, I would have to say that
sentences.zh: 我必须说，如果我完全坦诚的话，我必须说，我不得不说，

sentences.en: I'm somewhat surprised, as you seem to be, because I do think that what we're doing in many ways is sort of very serious and it's a very sober show.
sentences.zh: 我多少有点惊讶，正如你似乎也很惊讶一样，因为我确实认为我们在很多方面所做的事情非常严肃，这是一档非常冷静克制的节目。

sentences.en: We're focused on complex ideas and we're trying to sort of present complex ideas before people.
sentences.zh: 我们专注于复杂的理念，并试图将复杂的理念呈现在人们面前。

sentences.en: And like you, I think, you know, maybe 10 years ago, if you'd asked me how successful would a show like this be, I would say it would be modestly successful because the audience
sentences.zh: 我想就像你一样，你知道的，也许10年前，如果你问我这样一档节目会有多成功，我会说它会取得适度的成功，因为对于

sentences.en: for complexity and nuance is not very big.
sentences.zh: 复杂性和细微差别的受众并不是很大。

sentences.en: And I have to say that I've been surprised, pleasantly surprised at how popular a show like Hidden Brain is.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，对于《隐藏的大脑》这样一档节目有多受欢迎，我感到很惊讶，惊喜交加。

sentences.en: I think there are some things that we're doing that in fact are helpful, which is that we are constantly trying to connect the world of science with the world of storytelling and
sentences.zh: 我认为我们正在做的一些事情确实很有帮助，那就是我们不断地试图将科学世界与讲故事的世界联系起来，

sentences.en: trying to make stories as accessible and as interesting as possible.
sentences.zh: 并尽最大努力使故事尽可能平易近人和有趣。

sentences.en: I think we're genuinely interested and curious about the worlds in which we're covering.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对我们所报道的世界真正感兴趣并充满好奇。

sentences.en: And I think that enthusiasm comes through in the work that we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种热情体现在我们正在做的工作中。

sentences.en: I hope it comes through in just the conversation we're having right now.
sentences.zh: 我希望它体现在我们刚刚进行的这场对话中。

sentences.en: I hope people are hearing my own enthusiasm and passion for the fields that we cover.
sentences.zh: 我希望人们能听到我对我们所报道的领域的热情和热爱。

sentences.en: But also, I think podcasting in general has turned out to be this extraordinary gift because podcasting, of course, is fundamentally a business of niches.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我也认为播客总体上被证明是一份非凡的礼物，因为播客当然从根本上说是一个垂直细分（niche）的业务。

sentences.en: It's basically, are there enough people in this niche who are fascinated by what you're doing, that they're willing to actually listen to you?
sentences.zh: 它基本上是说，在这个细分领域里，是否有足够多的人对你正在做的事情着迷，以至于他们愿意真正听你讲？

sentences.en: And it turns out there, in fact, is a sizable number of people who are interested in thoughtful
sentences.zh: 事实证明，确实有相当数量的人对深思熟虑的

sentences.en: conversations, who are interested in nuance, who are interested in what their own minds are doing, who are interested in how they can modify and change how they're thinking and
sentences.zh: 对话感兴趣，对细微差别感兴趣，对他们自己的大脑在做什么感兴趣，对他们如何修改和改变他们的思维方式

sentences.en: how they should be responding to the world to have better relationships or perform better or function better at work or in their lives.
sentences.zh: 以及他们应如何回应世界以建立更好的关系或在工作中或生活中表现得更好或运转得更好感兴趣。

sentences.en: That audience turns out not to be trivial.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这个受众群体并不微不足道。

sentences.en: It turns out to be substantial.
sentences.zh: 事实证明它是相当可观的。

sentences.en: So, you know, I would say the short answer to your question, Kim, is the short answer really to how anyone gets successful, which is they work very hard and most of it is luck.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我会说对你问题的简短回答，金，实际上是对任何人如何取得成功的简短回答，那就是他们非常努力工作，而且很大程度上靠运气。

sentences.en: Well, Shankar Vedantam, thank you so much for speaking with me today.
sentences.zh: 好吧，尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam），非常感谢今天与我交谈。

sentences.en: This has been a great pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这真是一次非常愉快的交流。

sentences.en: Very happy to have some time with you.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴能有一些时间和您在一起。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: I'm a huge fan of everything that psychologists and the APA does, and I'm hugely grateful to the many scientists and researchers who share their time and insights with us.
sentences.zh: 我是心理学家和美国心理学协会（APA）所做一切的超级粉丝，我非常感谢与我们分享时间和见解的许多科学家和研究人员。

sentences.en: We wouldn't have a show without them.
sentences.zh: 如果没有他们，我们就不会有这档节目。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上，或者在苹果、Stitcher 或您获取播客的任何地方找到《心理学聊天》（Speaking of Psychology）先前的节目。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何评论或想法，可以通过电子邮件将意见发给我们，邮箱是 speakingofpsychology@APA.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学聊天》由李·韦纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Condayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬（Chris Condayan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening for the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 感谢您收听美国心理学协会的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
